sweep_summary: Wasa (wasa1244) is not in the catalog and this search of works with stress in the title turned up a single title-match: Kandybowicz & Torrence 2015 (ACAL 44, Cascadilla), which is open access and was downloaded and read in full with). It is a syntax-prosody paper on Intonational-Phrase mapping of embedded clauses in Krachi and Wasa (L% boundary tone, pause, pitch reset on a two-tone H/L system); it contains no word-stress or accent-placement statement and its footnote 1 says the authors could not locate any written materials on Wasa. Relevance: prosody-but-not-word-stress; bears on catalog: no-catalog-record; acquisition priority: none. No first-hand word-stress statement for Wasa was read, so no new stress statement was found. This matches an earlier compilation fullscan classification for this item (no source found). the Glottolog langdoc CSV endpoint returned a generic dump rather than a Wasa-specific list, and Ethnologue could not be reached by automated download. If a stress statement for Wasa is wanted, the nearest candidates would be Akan-cluster descriptions (e.g. Dolphyne 1988 on Twi-Fante sound systems and tone), which would be other-variety evidence, not Wasa-specific.

Zsiga & One Tlale Boyer (eds.), Selected Proceedings of the 44th Annual Conference on African Linguistics, 146-157. Somerville, MA: Cascadilla Proceedings Project.

sources.quote: For Wasa, we use a modified (non-IPA) version of the Akan script, as we have been unable to locate materials written in the language. [fn. 1, p. 147] ... Comparable phonetic correlates of right edge ι marking (i.e. L%, pause, pitch reset) exist in Wasa. This is demonstrated below by way of a clause modified by a reason adjunct. In this construction, the lexically H-bearing C0 sɛ at the right edge of ι surfaces with a depressed/falling F0. Following the complementizer is a pause. The range of F0 values following the break is also reset. [sec. 4.4, p. 154]
sources.locator: fn. 1, p. 147 (transcription conventions); sec. 4.4 'Prosodic status of Wasa embedded complement clauses', pp. 154-155
sources.note: Nothing. The paper is a syntax-prosody study of whether embedded complement clauses are mapped as Intonational Phrases (diagnosed by L% boundary tone on the H-toned complementizer, pause, and pitch reset); Wasa is handled as a two-tone (H/L) language with continuous F0 downdrift across clauses. The word 'stress' does not occur anywhere in the text; there is no statement of word-level stress or accent placement, and no phonological sketch of the word. Footnote 1 records that the authors could locate no written materials on Wasa at all.

sources.note: States (§1.3, p. 7) that Wassa is tonal with two basic tones, High and Low, every syllable bearing its own tone realized on vowels and syllabic consonants; abbreviations list H, L and downstep (!); the autosegmental framework chapter uses a tone tier, and the literature review (p. 29) summarizes Afful 2006: two basic tones, lexical and grammatical functions, H on the progressive marker and on monosyllabic verb TBUs in Wassa (like Bono, unlike Asante). The thesis body is about segmental processes (ATR harmony, palatalization, elision, consonant mutation), not a tonology.
